_doc: CLU-542. Searchable aliases: the names a person types that appear nowhere
in a list's title, subtitle, kind or year. Nathan's case was Grand Theft
Auto, which typing 'gta' did not find at all -- not ranked low, absent.
One file rather than an `aliases` field in each properties/*.json, for two
reasons. All 231 property files are written by a generator under tools/, so
a hand-edit there is content drift waiting to happen -- nine lists already
carry drift from one commit that edited property files without their
generators. And a collision is only visible when every alias is in one
place: the whole point of the `refused` map below is that it sits next to
the aliases it rules out. Same shape as tools/data/sequences.json, which
the build reads the same way.
src/build.py validates this file and copies it into properties/index.json
as an `aliases` array per list. The build FAILS on an unknown slug, on an
alias that is another list's real title, on an alias already inside its own
list's title (typing it already works), and on anything named in `refused`.
Rules for adding one:
- it must be a name people actually type. Not an invented nickname.
- lowercase, trimmed, two characters or more.
- do not repeat what the title already says. 'cap' finds Captain America
already; 'gta' finds nothing.
- prefer the punctuation-stripped form of a title people type in full:
'mash' for M*A*S*H, 'steins gate' for Steins;Gate, 'pokemon' for
Pokemon with the accent, 'hunter x hunter' for the multiplication sign.
- a substring of another alias is redundant: the ranker treats an alias
PREFIX as a name, so 'fate stay night' already answers to 'fate'.
- two lists may honestly share one alias ('spiderman' belongs to both
Spider-Man runs). The build prints every shared alias so it is reviewed
rather than discovered.

refused.ff: Final Fantasy and Fantastic Four both answer to it, and whichever list took it would be the wrong answer half the time.
refused.sw: Star Wars and Everything Dies: Secret Wars.
refused.bb: Breaking Bad and Bob's Burgers -- and Better Call Saul, which is inside the Breaking Bad list.
refused.green lantern: Lanterns is the Green Lantern show, but Green Lantern is another list's real title, and typing a list's name has to land on that list.
refused.mi: Mission: Impossible -- but Middle-earth's title already starts with it, and two letters that common is not a name.
refused.me: Mass Effect. Two letters that sit inside a hundred other words are noise.
refused.re: Resident Evil. Same problem: 're' is inside too much of the English language to mean anything.
refused.da: Dragon Age -- but 'da' already starts Daredevil and David Lynch.
refused.mia: Made in Abyss, against the ordinary English word.
refused.man of steel: a Snyder film. The Superman list here is the comics reading order, and sending that query to it would answer a different question.
refused.the dark knight: a Nolan film. The Batman list is the comics reading order.
